chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fadalah, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Sa'id, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who buys a garment and asks for a profit-sharing (murabahah) from him, which is seen as good in the sale of murabahah if he is truthful in the profit-sharing and specifies a profit of two danan or half a dirham, so he said, 'There is no harm.'

And he was asked about a man who bought goods in a group/bulk and asks for a profit-sharing from him on account of 'I bought them in a group,' so they say, 'How did you value them?' and he says, 'I valued this for such and that for such,' he said, 'There is no harm with it.'
I said, 'But they add to him more than what he valued,' he said, 'Unless they add to him more than what he valued.'

key_terms.مُرَابَحَة: Profit-sharing or adding a profit margin to a sale

ai.seo_question: Is profit-sharing (murabahah) permissible in Islamic trade if the profit amount is specified?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the permissibility of *murabahah* (cost-plus sale) provided the seller discloses the specific profit margin, such as two *danans* or half a dirham, ensuring transparency in the transaction. This ruling extends to bulk purchases where the seller itemizes the valuation, with the condition that the final agreed price does not exceed the disclosed cost-plus-profit structure, thereby preventing hidden usury (*riba*) while facilitating commercial flexibility.
